title: Lesson 6 - Choosing a Template Type from the Requirement: Bindings and Wrong-Type Traps
description: Identify the considerations for using a prompt template type such as field generation and flex types.

questions.question: A requirement is to generate an open-text product recommendation for an agent to use anywhere, drawing on an Account, its Cases, and a custom Asset object, invoked from an Apex action. Which type fits, and why?
options: Field Generation, because it writes to a record
Record Summary, because it summarizes records
Flex, because it defines its own resources, grounds with several objects, and is invoked from Flow, Apex, or a prompt action
Sales Email, because it grounds on a record
questions.explanation: The output is open text used anywhere, the prompt must read several objects, and the entry point is Apex, which together make Flex the only classic type whose binding and entry points fit.

questions.question: A scenario asks for a personalized renewal email to a Contact, with the prompt grounded in the Contact and one related object. Which type is correct?
options: Sales Email, which binds a Contact or a Lead and optionally one more object
Flex, because it is more flexible
questions.explanation: The output is a customer email and the anchor is a Contact, which is exactly the Sales Email binding, so a general type is unnecessary here.

questions.question: A requirement must combine six unrelated objects into one generated result. What is the correct reading?
options: Field Generation, because it writes to a record
Record Summary, because it reads the whole record
Sales Email, with the extra objects as related lists
Flex grounds with up to five objects, so a requirement needing more objects signals the prompt or its architecture needs rethinking
questions.explanation: Flex is the multi-object type and grounds with up to five objects, so exceeding that set points at a design problem rather than a different classic type with a wider binding.
